title: In 1861, Chicago Lifted a Hotel Six Feet. Guests Stayed Inside

scenes.text: In 1861, workers lifted a six story hotel with the guests still inside.
It was the Tremont House in Chicago, raised six feet on a thousand jackscrews.
Five hundred men turned the screws a little at a time.
One guest noticed the entrance steps getting steeper and the windows rising over his head.
The whole city was being raised, because it sat so low that sewage couldn't drain.
Chicago lifted itself out of the mud, one jackscrew at a time.

description:
In 1861, five hundred men used a thousand jackscrews to lift Chicago's six story Tremont House about six feet while guests stayed inside.
The city was raising whole streets because it sat so low that sewage could not drain.
Would you have stayed in the hotel? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: THEY LIFTED A HOTEL. GUESTS STAYED.
first_comment: Guests of the Tremont House kept sleeping while it rose. Would you have stayed?
